metadata.technology: Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor Probe (with MCU + radio)
metadata.technology_specification: Capacitive soil moisture sensor probe integrated with microcontroller unit (MCU) and wireless radio module
metadata.technology_reasoning: This type represents the industry-standard soil moisture sensor probe used in agriculture and environmental monitoring as of 2024, integrating capacitive sensing for soil moisture detection with an embedded MCU for signal processing and a radio module (often LoRa, BLE, or sub-GHz) for wireless communication to enable remote sensing and IoT applications.

components.reasoning: Core sensing element that measures soil moisture through changes in capacitance; universally present and critical.
Processes the sensor signal and controls data acquisition; standard embedded component in smart sensor probes.
Enables wireless communication of sensor data, typically LoRa, BLE, or sub-GHz, procured as a distinct module.

components.component: Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy Harvester)
components.reasoning: Provides power to the probe; often a dedicated battery pack or energy harvesting unit, sourced separately.
Houses the electronics including the MCU, radio, and sensor interface; a separate manufactured assembly.
Protects internal electronics and sensor elements from soil and moisture; essential structural component.
Facilitates radio communication; often a separate component optimized for wireless transmission.

Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensing Electro.name: Copper
Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensing Electro.reasoning: Copper is widely used for the conductive sensing electrodes due to its excellent electrical conductivity, essential for signal transmission and sensing.

Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensing Electro.name: Aluminum
Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensing Electro.reasoning: Aluminum can be used as an alternative conductive material for electrodes, offering good conductivity with lower cost, common in sensor electrodes.

Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensing Electro.name: Polyethylene terephthalate
Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensing Electro.reasoning: This polymer can serve as a flexible substrate or insulating layer for electrodes, common in sensor fabrication but alternatives exist.

Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensing Electro.name: Epoxy resins
Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensing Electro.reasoning: Used as an encapsulant or protective coating for stability and durability of the sensing electrode, commonly applied though other polymers can substitute.

Microcontroller Unit (MCU).name: Silicon
Microcontroller Unit (MCU).reasoning: Silicon is the fundamental semiconductor material for the integrated circuit die of MCUs, absolutely essential and standard in the industry.

Microcontroller Unit (MCU).name: Copper
Microcontroller Unit (MCU).reasoning: Copper is used for internal interconnects and wiring within the MCU chip package as well as in the lead frame, essential for electrical conductivity.

Microcontroller Unit (MCU).name: Aluminum
Microcontroller Unit (MCU).reasoning: Aluminum is commonly used for bonding wires inside the MCU package and sometimes for heat spreaders, a standard material though copper is also used.

Microcontroller Unit (MCU).name: Epoxy resins
Microcontroller Unit (MCU).reasoning: Epoxy resins are commonly used as encapsulants to protect the semiconductor die and bonding wires, essential for device reliability.

Wireless Radio Module.name: Silicon
Wireless Radio Module.reasoning: Silicon is essential as the semiconductor base material for RF IC chips in the radio module, universally used in modern radios.

Wireless Radio Module.name: Copper
Wireless Radio Module.reasoning: Copper is used extensively for wiring, interconnects, and antenna traces within the module due to its high conductivity.

Wireless Radio Module.name: Aluminum
Wireless Radio Module.reasoning: Used for casing and heat dissipation elements in the module, aluminum is standard and effective though alternatives exist.

Wireless Radio Module.name: Epoxy resins
Wireless Radio Module.reasoning: Used as encapsulants and adhesives within the module to protect components, very common in electronics packaging.

Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.name: Lithium
Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.reasoning: Lithium is critical for lithium-ion batteries which are widespread in power supply modules for wireless sensor devices, absolutely essential.

Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.name: Copper
Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.reasoning: Copper is essential for the current collectors and internal wiring of batteries and energy harvester circuits.

Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.name: Aluminum
Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.reasoning: Aluminum is used for cathode current collectors and packaging in batteries and as casing material in energy harvesters.

Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.name: Graphite
Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.reasoning: Graphite is commonly used as the anode material in lithium-ion batteries, critical for intercalation of lithium ions.

Printed Circuit Board (PCB).name: Copper
Printed Circuit Board (PCB).reasoning: Copper is the primary material for the conductive traces and pads on PCBs, indispensable for electrical connectivity.

Printed Circuit Board (PCB).name: Silicon dioxide
Printed Circuit Board (PCB).reasoning: Silicon dioxide is a key dielectric layer and insulating material on PCBs, commonly used as the substrate or part of substrate laminates.

Printed Circuit Board (PCB).name: Epoxy resins
Printed Circuit Board (PCB).reasoning: Used in the resin matrix of PCB laminates like FR-4, providing mechanical strength and insulation, industry standard.

Printed Circuit Board (PCB).name: Fiberglass
Printed Circuit Board (PCB).reasoning: Fiberglass fibers reinforce PCBs to provide mechanical stability and insulation, standard composite material in PCB fabrication.

Protective Housing/Enclosure.name: Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene
Protective Housing/Enclosure.reasoning: ABS plastic is commonly used for enclosures due to its mechanical strength, ease of molding, and weather resistance.

Protective Housing/Enclosure.name: Polycarbonate
Protective Housing/Enclosure.reasoning: Polycarbonate is another common enclosure material providing toughness, transparency, and UV resistance, widely used though more costly than ABS.

Protective Housing/Enclosure.name: Aluminum
Protective Housing/Enclosure.reasoning: Aluminum may be used for robust or heat dissipative housings, especially outdoors or rugged applications, though plastics dominate.

Antenna.name: Copper
Antenna.reasoning: Copper is the primary conductive material for antennas due to high electrical conductivity and ease of fabrication, essential for signal transmission.

Antenna.name: Aluminum
Antenna.reasoning: Aluminum is an alternative antenna material offering lower weight and cost, common in some antenna designs though less conductive than copper.

Antenna.name: Polyethylene terephthalate
Antenna.reasoning: Used as substrate material or protective layer in flexible antenna designs; various polymers can be used depending on flexibility and environmental protection needs.
